name: Shinjuku-Gyoemmae
tagline: Shinjuku in 3 minutes and Shibuya in 13 minutes. Served by 1 line. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000.
summary: The station is in Shinjuku City, where Tokyo Metro run 1 line between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 17 minutes to Otemachi, 3 minutes to Shinjuku, 13 minutes to Shibuya and 30 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. The station stands 34.1 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 4.1 m. The land around the station is close to level.

terrain.note: The station sits on the higher side of the ground around it, at 34.1 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 32.2 m to 36.3 m, a difference of 4.1 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, neither the station nor any of the nine points within 400 m of it falls inside the projected inundation area. On the whole, the flood projection here is among the smallest in the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 5 clinics and 9 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 仁圭会林外科病院, about 13 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 東京勤労者医療会代々木病院, about 15 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 1 line serve the station: Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line runs at 154% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 新大塚→茗荷谷, which this station is not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥140,000 to ¥150,000 and 1K ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. 1LDK ¥220,000 to ¥230,000 and 2LDK ¥330,000 to ¥340,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

Whether it faces a main road or the railway

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥140,000 to ¥150,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is about average for the 23 wards. a small projected flood depth pushes the figure up. On the other side, only one line, the {line}, serving the station and little daily shopping within walking distance holds it down. For 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: For the number of medical facilities, Shinjuku-Sanchome; for how little of the area is in the flood projection, Shinjuku-Gyoemmae.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Shinjuku-Gyoemmae. Both have the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line. Shinjuku-Sanchome also has the Tokyo Metro Fukutoshin Line and Toei Shinjuku Line, which Shinjuku-Gyoemmae does not. Shinjuku-Sanchome is 5 minutes quicker to Shibuya, but times to the other main business districts are much the same. On the number of medical facilities, Shinjuku-Sanchome comes out ahead. Within about 13 minutes' walk, Shinjuku-Sanchome has 52 clinics and pharmacies and Shinjuku-Gyoemmae has 14.

neighbours.lead: For lower rent, Sendagaya; for how close the centre is, Shinjuku-Gyoemmae.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Shinjuku-Gyoemmae. Shinjuku-Gyoemmae adds the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line; Sendagaya adds the JR Chuo-Sobu Line (Local). Shinjuku-Gyoemmae is at least 5 minutes quicker to Toranomon and Otemachi. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥11,000 less at Sendagaya.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
People who get around by bicycle or with a pushchair
People who want a large park within walking distance
People avoiding projected flood inundation areas
notFor: People who want another route when service is suspended
People who want to finish their shopping on foot
noiseSources: The nearest big road, 靖国通り, is far enough that little traffic noise reaches the station area

leads.terrain: The ground around the station is almost level, so you can choose where to live without thinking about slopes.
leads.groceries: There are 4 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 8 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: Neither the station nor the ground around it falls inside the projected flood area.
leads.stationNote: Only the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line serves this station, so when it stops you walk to another station.
leads.rentRange: The balance between commuting time and rent is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Mornings here are less crowded than the line figures suggest: the lines are busy, but this station is outside their busiest stretches.
leads.noiseSources: The big roads are far enough that traffic noise is unlikely to bother you.
